Why does the hypergeometric theorem imply that the sum from k=0 to n of p(k) equals 1? Choices: A) Dividing both sides of C(N,n) = Σ C(m,k)·C(N-m,n-k) by C(N,n) gives 1 = Σ p(k) | B) Because every p(k) is greater than or equal to 0 | C) Because N = m + n | D) Because C(N,n) = N! Answer with the letter only.
Hints: Look at what happens when the identity is divided by C(N,n)
Solution: Dividing the identity by $\binom{N}{n}$ turns each term into $p(k)$ and the left side into $1$. The answer is A.
